subChunks.title: CAST and Type Conversion
subChunks.hookHtml: Data stored in one type often needs to be treated as another. CAST makes the conversion explicit and portable.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
CAST syntax

SELECT CAST(xp AS REAL) / 100 AS xp_hundreds FROM apprentices;
SELECT CAST('2024-03-15' AS DATE) AS parsed_date;
SELECT CAST(42 AS TEXT) AS str_val;

:: shorthand (PostgreSQL)

SELECT xp::REAL / 100 FROM apprentices;
SELECT '2024-03-15'::DATE;

PostgreSQL-specific but very common in practice. Use CAST for portability.

Implicit vs explicit conversion

SQL engines convert types implicitly in many situations (e.g. comparing INTEGER 5 with TEXT '5' may work in MySQL). Relying on implicit conversion leads to subtle bugs — always cast explicitly when mixing types.

String to number

SELECT CAST('1234' AS INTEGER) + 1;  -- 1235
-- Fails if the string is not a valid number:
SELECT CAST('abc' AS INTEGER);       -- error in strict engines

Common use cases

  • Integer division → float: CAST(a AS REAL) / b
  • Concatenating number + text: CAST(xp AS TEXT) || ' XP'
  • Formatting output: CAST(score AS DECIMAL(5,2))

storyBeats.text: The XP column is INTEGER. The average needs decimal precision. CAST bridges the gap.

storyBeats.speaker: Cipher the Archivist
storyBeats.text: CAST is explicit — it makes your intentions clear to the engine and to the next reader. Implicit conversions are convenient until they silently produce the wrong result. Make the conversion visible; do not trust the engine to guess correctly.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
🪄 XP percentage

Return name and each apprentice's XP as a percentage of the maximum XP in the table, rounded to one decimal place, aliased as pct. Use CAST for the division.
subChunks.guidedPracticeStarterCode:
SELECT
  name,
  ROUND(
    CAST(xp AS REAL) / (SELECT MAX(xp) FROM apprentices) * 100,
    1
  ) AS pct
FROM apprentices
ORDER BY pct DESC;

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain why explicit CAST is better than relying on implicit type conversion, and give an example where implicit conversion produces a wrong result.

questions.explanation: Casting 7 to REAL before dividing makes the division floating-point. REAL / INTEGER = REAL result, giving 3.5.

questions.prompt: Which query concatenates a number and text portably?
questions.explanation: CAST to TEXT with || is standard SQL. xp + ' XP' is a type error in strict engines. :: is PostgreSQL-specific. CONCAT works in MySQL/PostgreSQL but not SQLite.

questions.prompt: What does `CAST('abc' AS INTEGER)` return in a strict SQL engine?
options: An error — 'abc' cannot be converted to an integer
questions.answer: An error — 'abc' cannot be converted to an integer
questions.explanation: Strict engines (PostgreSQL) raise an error when a string cannot be parsed as the target type. Lenient engines (SQLite) may return NULL. Always validate input before casting user-provided strings.

questions.prompt: MySQL implicitly converts when comparing `WHERE id = '5'` (id is INTEGER). Why is this dangerous?
options: It works now but may fail on engine version changes, and the implicit conversion prevents index use if the plan changes
The integer is converted to a string and string comparison is performed
NULL values are not handled correctly
questions.answer: It works now but may fail on engine version changes, and the implicit conversion prevents index use if the plan changes
questions.explanation: Implicit conversions are engine-defined behaviour that can change. They can also prevent optimal index use. Always compare like types: WHERE id = 5 (not '5') when id is INTEGER.
